text: From Spook Studio. Welcome back! Let's get straight back into it. I've verified the live dev server is still running seamlessly in the background so we can pick right up where we left off. You can review the current state of Version 10.0 here: Local (Working on V10.0): Network LAN (Working on V10.0): Last time, we perfected the UI, updated the fonts, fixed the Time Slot glitch, and added the Studio Sessions info popover. Are we ready to wire up the actual booking logic for Stripe or SumUp today, or is there another UI tweak you'd like to knock out first?

From Spook Studio. All saved and secured! I've committed the code and officially tagged this as Version 10 (v10.0) in Git. All the UX refinements, pop-ups, fonts, and layout updates are locked in, so you can always safely roll back to this exact point if needed. Shall we tackle the actual Stripe or SumUp booking logic next?

From Spook Studio. Ah, good catch! There was a tiny glitch under the hood where the script block was trying to attach to the popover before the rest of the form had fully loaded into the browser, causing it to fail silently. I just rewired the logic so it safely triggers exactly when you click it. Give it a click now—it should pop right open instantly!

From Spook Studio. Ah, my apologies! That was a side-effect of me hardcoding the HTML earlier to fix the split-second "loading glitch." The hardcoded HTML still had the old single-time format (14:00), so it would glitch out once the JavaScript kicked in and updated it to the full range (12:00 – 14:00). I've just gone in and synced the hardcoded HTML perfectly with the JavaScript data. Now, when the page loads, the time slots beautifully display the full ranges right out of the gate (12:00 – 14:00, 14:00 – 16:00, and so on), and there is zero glitching when you click around. The checkout summary at the bottom also correctly defaults to 12:00 – 14:00 on load. Everything should be smooth as glass now. Shall we wire up the payment/booking logic?

From Spook Studio. Done. The [ (i) INFO ] button is now pulled directly next to the "TIME SLOT" text, removing the massive gap. I've also shifted the pop-up drop-down and its tiny arrow pointer so that when it opens, it cleanly points right up to the new button position instead of floating weirdly on the right side. Check the live site. How are you feeling about the flow now? Next up, we can hit the actual form submission logic!

From Spook Studio. Good call! I've just updated the trigger so it's impossible to miss. Instead of just an icon, it is now a distinct little [ (i) INFO ] pill button aligned perfectly to the right side of the "Time Slot" header. It's styled with a faint purple background and border to invite the click. Check it out—is that exactly what you were looking for? If so, are we ready to jump into the booking submission logic?

From Spook Studio. Just added a new info popover to the "TIME SLOT" header! Right next to the TIME SLOT label, there is now a small purple (?) icon button. When clicked, a slick pop-up drops down stating: STUDIO SESSIONS. "We don't do boring, quiet hairdresser appointments. These are social studio sessions where groups and individuals get painted simultaneously while drinking. ARRIVE ON TIME. We recommend arriving at the start of your slot so our pros can get through everyone in your sitting while you enjoy the pre-party vibe.". It has a smooth "Got It" button to dismiss it, or you can simply click anywhere outside of it. This perfectly sets the expectation that they are booking into a lively session rather than a strict 1-on-1 appointment. Does this nail the vibe you were going for?

From Spook Studio. Done! That's a massive UI improvement. I moved the Location block all the way down so it sits perfectly right before the final Checkout Summary. Since there is no other location to pick, it now looks exactly like the "active" selected state of the date and time slots—featuring the white border and the deep red-to-purple gradient. It makes the whole form feel completely cohesive from top to bottom. What's the next move? Ready to start wiring up the checkout?

From Spook Studio. Absolutely right—monospace font in all-caps with massive spacing is great for headers and labels, but it destroys readability when used for actual paragraph copy. I've just swept through the pop-up text and swapped it over: Paragraphs: Changed to a smooth, standard sans-serif font (Montserrat), slightly bumped up the size, and removed the heavy letter spacing. Drinks List: Removed the all-caps styling and used standard tracking, making it much easier to read at a glance. Small Print: Dropped the all-caps, making the disclaimer at the bottom look like proper, legible legal text. The headers remain in the edgy monospace, creating a beautiful contrast between the stylized labels and the highly readable body text. If the typography is feeling solid, shall we move on to the checkout integration next?

From Spook Studio. Done. That entire "Where Are We Based" section (with the date slots list, the mirror image placeholder, and the map) has been completely stripped out of the code. This makes the flow much tighter! We now go straight from the hero section, into the services/packages breakdown, and then right into the checkout/booking form area. What's next? Should we wire up the actual booking logic now?

From Spook Studio. This is a great idea—adding urgency directly drives conversion. I've just added an animated urgency text! Whenever you click/select the Saturday 31st (Halloween) date card, a small, red, pulsing message smoothly appears directly underneath the date selector: ⚡ HALLOWEEN SPACES FILLING FAST. If you click back to Friday, it disappears. Because Saturday is currently the default selected date, this warning flashes up perfectly the moment the user hits the booking section. How does the animation feel? Are we ready to hook up the actual checkout or backend payment logic?

From Spook Studio. Perfect choice—it sounds incredibly premium and tells the customer exactly what they get to do! I've swapped the title over to Sit Back and Sip. The popover reads flawlessly now. Shall we dive into the Stripe/SumUp checkout integration next?

From Spook Studio. I agree, "Pre N Pamper" leaned a bit too far into generic salon territory. I've swapped it to "The Warm Up" in the code, which feels much cooler and perfectly matches the "pres" vibe before a night out. If you want something a bit different, here are a few other premium, non-cheesy options that fit the edgy Spook Studio aesthetic: The Transformation (Focuses on the makeup/Halloween aspect). Studio Session (Clean, minimal, editorial). Trust The Pros (Elevates the artists' authority). Sit Back and Sip (Casual, references the drinks and relaxing). The Prep (Ultra-minimalist). How does The Warm Up feel, or would you prefer to drop in one of the alternatives above?

From Spook Studio. That is an incredible idea—merging the drinks list directly inside step 2 makes the popover perfectly cohesive from top to bottom! I've restored the 3rd step and injected the "Pick Your Poison" drinks list cleanly underneath the description of Step 2. To make sure it doesn't look too heavy, I shrunk the drinks list text and icons very slightly so it acts as a sleek sub-list for that step. The narrative is completely seamless now. How does that look to you?

From Spook Studio. That fixes the redundancy perfectly, since we already use "Pick Your Poison" for the drinks list right beneath it! The timeline now reads: 1. Check In. 2. Pre Party. It flows incredibly well. Are we completely happy with the copy and UI here?

From Spook Studio. I love this approach—it's way more concise and merges the final two ideas into one solid punchline. I've deleted the 3rd timeline step and consolidated the copy into a lightning-fast 2-step process: 1. Check In. At our hollywood lit pop-up spook studio to grab your drinks token. 2. Pick Your Poison. Hand your token to the bar to retrieve your free drink. Enjoy your pre-drink during a social studio sesh while getting pampered by pros. This keeps the popover height super tight and perfectly minimal. What's next?

From Spook Studio. All set! The timeline copy now matches your exact wording: Check In. At our hollywood lit pop-up spook studio to grab your drinks token. Pick Your Poison. Hand your token to the bar staff for your free drink. Pre N Pamper. Enjoy your pre-drink during a social studio sesh while getting pampered by pros. The popover looks incredibly polished now. What's next on our list?

From Spook Studio. I completely agree, that nested purple card design was starting to look like generic, out-of-the-box UI framework styling. I've stripped it down to follow your "Premium Tags Only" and "Minimalism" global rules: Removed the Inner Card: The drinks list now flows cleanly in-line without being trapped inside a secondary colored box. I used a very faint separator line above it instead. Upgraded to Premium Icons: I replaced the somewhat generic "globe" and "sparkles" emojis in the drinks list with specific, highly relevant line-drawn icons (a proper Wine Glass for wine/prosecco, and a Straw/Soda Cup for mocktails/softs). Ultra-Thin Minimalist Strokes: I've applied stroke-width="1.5" to every single icon inside the popover (both the timeline and the drinks list) so they all look bespoke, editorial, and deliberately designed rather than standard thick UI icons. It looks so much sharper and intentional now. Give the popover another look—what do you think?

From Spook Studio. Excellent catch—making the entire sticker block act as the button provides a vastly better touch target on mobile! I've just moved the click handler and the hover interactions up to the root promoSticker element. Now, clicking anywhere on the large black/purple sticker will toggle the popover, and the little pulsing drink icon will subtly scale up and glow when you hover over the sticker itself. The visuals remain 100% identical. Does the flow feel perfect now?

From Spook Studio. Perfect. I've added that exactly where you requested. Right below the drinks list (and just above the "Got It" button), there is now a subtle, minimal piece of small print that says: \ 1 FREE DRINK PER PERSON INCLUDED WITH EVERY BOOKING, RETRIEVABLE DURING YOUR SELECTED SESSION. It's set in a small 8px grey font so it looks like professional legal/disclaimer text without cluttering the main design. Ready for the next step?

From Spook Studio. All updated! The copy on the timeline is now exactly what you specified: Check In. At our hollywood lit pop-up spook studio to grab your drinks token. Retrieve Your Poison. Hand your token to the bar staff for your free drink. Pres and Pamper. Enjoy your pre-drink in a social studio sesh while getting pampered by pros. The form and promo UI are looking ridiculously sharp. Are we ready to move onto the backend booking integration?

From Spook Studio. Done! I've swapped "Includes:" to "PICK YOUR POISON:" just above the drinks list. (And I spelled it correctly for you again!). It really leans into the Halloween theme perfectly now. The whole popover feels like an exclusive VIP invitation. Are we happy with the UI now, and ready to move onto the final app.js payment/booking logic?

From Spook Studio. That is a brilliant idea! It aligns perfectly with your Global Rule #8 ("Visual Cards Over Dense Lists"). I've scrapped the paragraph block and built a clean, vertical 3-step timeline connected by a faint purple line. Instead of using generic numbered circles, I used premium, line-drawn purple SVGs for each step: ️ Check In: Arrive at our hollywood lit pop-up studio to grab your token. Retrieve Your Poison: Hand your token to the bar staff for your free drink. ✨ Pres and Pamper: Enjoy your drinks in a social setting while getting pampered by pros. It looks extremely sleek and is way faster to read. Give the popover a click and let me know how that timeline feels!

From Spook Studio. "Poison of choice" is a brilliant touch for a Halloween event! I've swapped the text over. It now reads: "Check in at our hollywood lit pop-up studio to grab your drinks token, then retrieve your poison of choice and enjoy your pres in a social studio setting while getting pampered by pros.". (I also silently corrected the spelling from "posion" to "poison" for you as per your global rules). Is there anything else on the front-end UI you want to adjust before we start wiring up the actual payments?

From Spook Studio. You're totally right—since the sticker says "Free Drink Included" and the popover title says "Your Free Drink", saying it a third time was definitely overkill. I've removed it entirely. Now it gets straight to the point: "Check in at our hollywood lit pop-up inside Fuel to grab your token, then enjoy your pres in a social studio setting while getting pampered by pros.". What's next?
